Every man ostracised in ancient Athens w.why: The defining term of the procedure, given in the first sentence of the Wikipedia article and in every account of it. No exception: men recalled early (Aristides, Xanthippus, Cimon) had still been sentenced to ten years, which is why the rule speaks of the sentence.

notes: Dev TBox revision: the rule is the defining term of Athenian ostracism (ten years' exile), held by every model and without exception once stated as the sentence; the revision halves it. The three derived queries name an ostracised man the model has almost certainly stored nothing about by name (Hipparchus son of Charmus, Megacles son of Hippocrates, Menon son of Meneclides, from Wikipedia's list of known ostracisms) and state the membership in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops). The well-known victims (Aristides, Themistocles, Cimon) are not asked. The first asks the term (answer); the other two use it in a small computation (application, fol arithmetic): whether the sentence had run out seven years after he left (no, then yes) and his age when it ended if he left at 40 (50, then 45). Both avoid counting in BC years, where models count the wrong way. Near unrelated asks another Athenian sentence (Socrates': death). The relation sentenced_to_exile_for is catalogued in staging/history.RELATIONS.md. Every bridge is stated in its prompt, so only the side facts have checks.
